Set search query '苏绣' on homepage, opened suzhou-embroidery detail page, navigated back via browser back button; search input value remained '苏绣' and result count remained '共 1 个非遗项目'.

Clicking loaded hotspot 'suzhou-embroidery' opens panorama.overlay containing image(s), title '苏绣', category '传统工艺', region '江苏 · 江南水乡', brief description text, and a '查看详情' link targeting heritage.detail.

issue: Hotspots are permanently lost after sufficient panorama rotation instead of reappearing as the view wraps around
actual: Starting with 4 visible hotspots, incrementally dragging the panorama (background gradient rotation angle moved continuously from 135deg through 93/56/19/-41/-130 down to -250.8deg, i.e. over 385 degrees of cumulative rotation, more than a full 360deg lap) caused the visible hotspot count to shrink from 4 to 2 to 0, and it never recovered even after the cumulative rotation exceeded 360 degrees and reversing direction with multiple drags of equal/larger magnitude. Only a full page reload restored the 4 hotspots. Zooming in/out alone did not permanently lose hotspots (they reappeared on zoom-out), but sustained drag-rotation permanently empties the hotspot set with no recovery via further dragging in either direction.
evidence: Sequence of panorama.hotspots.item counts observed while dragging: 4→4(diff set)→4→2→0(at translateX=130.8px, angle108.84→ eventually 93.45)→0 through translateX up to 1929px / angle -250.8deg, hotspots array remained empty ([]) for the rest of the test.

Set panorama zoom to scale(1.4) and rotation to translateX(37.35px)/gradient 127.53deg, then opened suzhou-embroidery hotspot overlay, navigated to its detail page via '查看详情', and used browser back navigation. On return, the panorama transform was exactly restored: 'transform: scale(1.4) rotateX(0deg) translateX(37.35px)' with identical gradient angle 127.53deg.
